facts.value: origin disputed. Tradition names Maro (d. c. 400)

citations.excerpt: We are told of an early Antiochene, Mar Marun or Maro, who died about A.D. 400 in the odour of sanctity in a convent at Ribla on the Orontes, whence orthodoxy spread over mid-Syria. But nothing sure is known of him

disagreements.value: The Maronite tradition holds an unbroken orthodox patriarchal line from John Maro
disagreements.excerpt: these patriarchs , never having erred in faith , or strayed into schism , are the only legitimate heirs of the Patriarchate of Antioch

disagreements.value: EB1911 holds the early patriarchs were Monothelite for about 500 years
disagreements.excerpt: their first patriarch and his successors, for about 500 years at any rate, were Monothelite, and perhaps also Monophysite.

facts.value_before_verify: origin disputed. Tradition names Maro (d. c. 400) and John Maro (d. 707)

citations.excerpt: In 1182 it is said that Amaury, patriarch of Antioch, induced some Maronite bishops, who had fallen under crusading influences, to rally to Rome; and a definite acceptance of the Maronite Church into the Roman communion took place at the Council of Florence in 1445.

facts.value: In communion with Rome while keeping a Syriac liturgy and a non-celibate priesthood. Accepted a constitution from Rome at the Council of Lowaizi, 1736.

citations.excerpt: at a council held at the monastery of Lowaizi on the 30th of September 1736, the Maronite Church accepted from Rome a constitution which is still in force
It retained, however, its Syriac liturgy and a non-celibate priesthood.

facts.value_before_verify: In communion with Rome while keeping a Syriac liturgy and married priests. Accepted a constitution from Rome at the Council of Lowaizi, 1736.

facts.value: An Eastern Catholic church whose home is Mount Lebanon.

citations.excerpt: a Christian people of the Ottoman Empire in communion with the Papal Church, but forming a distinct denomination. The original seat and present home of the nucleus of the Maronites is Mt Lebanon
